insight: Only a trace of rain has fallen recently (1.5 mm) — very little rain, and too little to drive meaningful runoff. The model's main signals right now: high tide level is lowering risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; only 1.5 mm of rain has fallen — very little rain, not enough to drive meaningful runoff; and high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach. The last lab sample (20 MPN/100mL) is now 29 days old — beaches are sampled about weekly, so a reading this stale carries little weight, and this estimate leans on current conditions.
